Such descriptions will be entered as endorsements and, taken together with the graphical representation, will help to define the scope of the registration."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3#1","quote":"Additionally, in the case of a trade mark that consists of or contains a sign that is a colour, scent, shape, sound, aspect of packaging or other kind of non-traditional sign, the application must include a concise and accurate description of the trade mark (subreg 4.3(7))."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/4","quote":"In most cases the applicant will need to file a copy of the actual sound being claimed as the trade mark. This copy should be provided on a medium which allows for easy copying, storage and replaying of the sound. CDs, DVDs and digital sound files are all suitable media."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/4","quote":"If it is not possible to provide the actual sound at the time of filing, for example, when the applicant experiences difficulties in attaching a sound file to an electronically filed application, the medium incorporating the sound should be sent to the Office as soon as possible after the application is filed."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3","quote":"The representation of the trade mark may consist of a written description of sounds if the sign is not a musical-type sound."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3","quote":"A sign consisting of a musical sound might be most appropriately represented in the form of musical notation, however, this will depend on the trade mark."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/1","quote":"An actual sample of the trade mark may be required for three dimensional shape trade marks."}],"answer":"**Fees to bodies other than IP Australia:** The supplied passages do not answer whether any such payments are required. I cannot establish that from these sources. The Manual only says that processing and fees vary depending on the filing method (TMM/Part5/2/2/2~1).

**Representation — Act and Manual practice:** Section 27(3)(a) of the Act requires a representation of the trade mark. Section 40 requires rejection if the mark cannot be represented graphically. Separately, the Registrar’s Manual practice is to require a graphical representation in the application (TMA1995/s27(3)(a); TMA1995/s40; TMM/Part10/3/3/1).

**Description — Manual guidance referring to the Regulations:** For a mark consisting of or containing a colour, scent, shape, sound, aspect of packaging or other non-traditional sign, include a concise and accurate description. The Manual attributes this requirement to subregulation 4.3(7), but the Regulations text itself has not been supplied. Under Manual practice, the description is entered as an endorsement and helps define the registration’s scope together with the graphical representation (TMM/Part10/3#1; TMM/Part10/3/3/1).

**Sound marks — Manual practice:** In most cases, provide a copy of the actual sound on a medium allowing easy copying, storage and replaying: a digital sound file, CD or DVD. If you cannot provide it at filing, send it to the Office as soon as possible afterwards. For the graphical representation, a non-musical sound may be represented by a written description; musical notation may be appropriate for a musical sound, depending on the mark (TMM/Part10/3/3/3/4; TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3).

**Three-dimensional shape marks — Manual practice:** An actual sample may also be required; the passage does not make this mandatory in every case (TMM/Part10/3/3/1)."}
